table.title: Import and Export of Gold, Silver and Merchandise, 1916 to 1927
table.caption_extra: In thousands of Haikwan taels (000 omitted.)
transcriber_notes: Table printed sideways (rotated); read from rotated crops.
Title says 1916 to 1927 but rows printed are 1918-1927 only.
Last row is an unlabelled totals row (stub blank as printed); the Merchandise Net Export cell in it is printed as a short dash '--', transcribed as '—'.
Every year row checks: Imported - Exported = Net Import/Net Export for gold and silver, and Merchandise Net Import - Net Export = Excess of Import.
Gold total net export 15,048: sum of net exports 74,354 minus net imports 45,306 = 15,048 — reconciles.
Silver total net import 515,274: parts sum to 515,274 — reconciles.
Merchandise total excess of import 1,843,504: parts sum to 1,843,504 — reconciles.

table.title: Movement of Silver to and from China
table.caption_extra: TREASURE. (Figures in Haikwan taels.) Compiled from statistics published by the Chinese Maritime Customs for the period from 1901 to 1927 inclusive.
transcriber_notes: Table printed sideways; read from rotated, enlarged crops. The year column is printed at both left and right edges; both kept.
Last row is the printed totals line (no stub label printed; '[Total]' supplied). Totals are printed with a '$' sign although the table is in Haikwan taels.
Row checks (Bars & Sycee + Coin = Total; Total imports - Total exports = Net Imports/Net Exports) hold for every year except:
1915 Exports: Bars & Sycee + Coin = 38,199,820 vs printed Total 39,099,820 — does NOT reconcile (diff 900,000)
1915: Export total - Import total = 18,382,314 vs printed Net Exports 18,882,314 — does NOT reconcile
1925 Imports: Bars & Sycee + Coin = 100,926,595 vs printed Total 73,926,595 — does NOT reconcile (diff -27,000,000)

1925 imports: Bars & Sycee printed 96,273,547 (re-read at high zoom); a figure of 69,273,547 would reconcile with the printed Total 73,926,595 and with Net Imports 62,523,626 — likely transposed digits in print; not corrected.
1915 exports: re-read at high zoom; Total 39,099,820 and Net Exports 18,882,314 are each 900,000/500,000 off the parts as printed; not corrected.
Net Imports total $734,128,959: column parts sum to 637,429,648 — does NOT reconcile (diff 96,699,311).
Net Exports total $190,613,131: column parts sum to 191,113,131 — does NOT reconcile (diff -500,000; the 1915 figure 18,882,314 is 500,000 above what the export/import totals give).

transcriber_notes: Table printed sideways across pp. 303-304; read from rotated crops. The 'Asia:—' heading row has blank cells.

As printed, the Imports half (p. 303) has the stub heading 'Countries to which Exported' and total line 'Total Exports', and the Exports half (p. 304) has 'Countries from which Imported' and 'Total Imports' — the stub labels appear transposed in print; transcribed as printed. The p. 303 totals match the 1927 import figures of the gold and silver movement tables (pp. 301-302) and the p. 304 totals match the 1927 export figures.
Several nil entries are printed as very short or faint dashes (e.g. Exports: Europe silver and copper cells); all transcribed as '—'.
Every row check (gold parts = gold total; silver parts = silver total; gold total + silver total + copper = grand total) and every column total reconciles in both halves.
